title: Tests of Unsaturation and Comparative Properties
topicTitle: Test of unsaturation (ethene and ethyne): bromine water test and Baeyer's test; comparative studies of physical properties of alkane, alkene and alkyne; Kolbe's electrolysis methods
notes: **Bromine water test:** unsaturation decolourises orange-brown bromine water: $CH_2=CH_2 + Br_2 \rightarrow CH_2Br-CH_2Br$ (colourless). Alkanes do not react.

**Baeyer's test (alkaline $KMnO_4$):** unsaturation decolourises purple permanganate, forming brown $MnO_2$ precipitate and diol: $RCH=CHR' + KMnO_4 + H_2O \rightarrow RCH(OH)-CH(OH)R' + MnO_2 + KOH$.

**Physical properties trend:** boiling points: alkynes > alkenes > alkanes (same C number) because of increased polarizability. Solubility: all non-polar, insoluble in water, soluble in organic solvents.

**Kolbe's electrolysis:** electrolysis of sodium or potassium salt of carboxylic acid gives alkane at cathode and alkene/alkyne at anode depending on conditions: $2RCOONa \xrightarrow{electrolysis} R-R + 2CO_2 + 2NaOH$.
**Density:** increases with unsaturation. Acetylene (1.17 g/L) > ethylene (1.25? actually 1.178) > ethane (1.26? at STP, but trend is not simple due to molecular weight differences).
